job.title: Research Analyst
job.location: Kampala, Uganda GROSS SALARY RANGE: $2, 979 - $4, 092(gross monthly) Laterite is looking for a new Research Analyst with an understanding of data analysis and a strong motivation to work in social and economic research to join our office in Kampala, Uganda. This role combines research design, data analysis, project management support, data quality analysis, and fieldwork coordination in a collaborative and fast-paced environment. WHO WE ARE Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others. We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2, 000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles. THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO You will join our team in Uganda in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with. Laterite was founded in 2010 in Kigali, and our office in Kampala opened in 2018. Our project portfolio in Uganda is varied across multiple sectors, and ranges from data collection studies, where Laterite manages data collection for our clients, to full-cycle research projects, where Laterite is responsible for evaluation and sampling methodology, survey design and coding, data collection, data quality and analysis. The Uganda team has managed some of our largest data collection projects and phone surveys on topics spanning coffee agronomy, foundational learning and education, sexual and reproductive health, and renewable energy. Our team in Uganda currently consists of 5 team members. TEAM STRUCTURE You will report to the Research Manager and Uganda country lead, working closely with the research operations team and data quality colleagues across Laterite. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with research team members in other country offices HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT 1 Supporting research projects Support the ethical approval process, research design, and development of research instruments, Conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis. Draft sections of reports and presentations for clients. Support communication with clients and internal project teams on project progress. 2 Contributing to data collection Code survey instruments using SurveyCTO and other ODK-based platforms. Collaborate with field teams to develop training materials and support enumerator trainings. Participate in field visits to understand and improve data collection processes. 3 Strengthening data quality and analysis Monitor, clean, and validate incoming survey data (by conducting high-frequency checks, for example). Work closely with field teams to resolve data quality issues. Support statistical analysis and interpretation of findings. Contribute to consultancy-quality reports and data-driven insights. 4 Contributing to business development (Optional) If you are interested, there is also room to contribute to our business development efforts, either through proactive business development or by contributing to the development of technical and financial proposals. WHAT YOU BRING We are looking for a colleague with strong quantitative data analysis skills and a motivation to work on socio-economic development research. Specifically, you have: A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Public Health, Development, statistics, or related fields. At least one year of professional experience in similar roles or tasks. (We welcome experience gained through internships, dissertation work, or participation in an academic research group, provided you can demonstrate how this experience meets the requirements of the role.) Strong quantitative data analysis skills and proficiency in Stata. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. In addition, we welcome: Experience working with ODK-based platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO). Previous work experience in Uganda Additional software skills, such as knowledge of R or Python. Organizational and interpersonal skills, self-motivation and drive to work in a collaborative environment. WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND DEVELOP Technical research design, including sampling and impact evaluation methodologies. Project management and client communication. Advanced data analysis, statistical techniques, and coding skills. Report writing and presentation of findings in a consultancy-quality format. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU Competitive compensation. $2, 092 gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 21 days of annual leave. Professional growth. We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to $1, 000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year. Flexibility. We also provide remote work options in accordance with Laterite’s remote work policy. How to apply READY TO BUILD WITH US? NEXT STEPS Online assessment. job.location: Kampala (Uganda)-based, with frequent travels to Sudan (Khartoum – security situation dependent), Northern Uganda (Kiryadongo), South Sudan (Juba) and Chad (Adré). Availability : Full-time commitment Period: Individual consultancy contract 12 months, starting 1 December 2026, renewable based on performance. Reporting to: Voice Programme Manager About Us The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation (MF) is an international rights-based, survivor-centred organisation, dedicated to ending sexual violence as a weapon of war globally. The Mukwege Foundation supports survivors’ demands for a world where sexual violence as a weapon of war is no longer tolerated, and bears consequences for individual perpetrators and states. We work for a future where survivors receive the holistic care and compensation they need to rebuild their lives. We create opportunities for survivors to speak out and be heard, and where they can organise to create change, influence policies, and demand justice and accountability. The Mukwege Foundation’s ‘Voice’ programme focuses on strengthening survivors’ agency to actively influence and participate in policy and practice concerning them at national and international levels. At the global level, SEMA – the Global Network of Victims and Survivors to End Wartime Sexual Violence – offers a safe global platform for survivors to come together for solidarity, to share experiences and knowledge, to advocate powerfully for the abolition of the use of sexual violence as a tactic of war, and to lobby for the recognition of the rights of survivors to quality holistic care and to restorative justice. At the national level, the Mukwege Foundation supports the initiation, development, and strengthening of in-country survivor networks, creating safe spaces for peer-to-peer support and building survivors’ capacities to enable them to actively engage in advocating for their rights. The in-country networks vary according to their context and capacities, but in all cases these networks organize to raise awareness about the reality, causes and consequences of wartime rape in the respective countries, to combat stigma, impunity and harmful myths around CRSV, to increase access to survivor-centred holistic care and to commemorate and recognize the many victims of these atrocities by creating a collective memory of survivors’ experiences. The Mukwege Foundation is currently supporting national survivor networks in Bangladesh, Central African Republic, Ethiopia, Iraq, Mali, Myanmar, Nigeria, Nepal, Syria, South Sudan, Uganda, Ukraine, and is in the process of expanding its programme to Chad and Sudan in 2026. Background The conflict in Sudan has been characterised by widespread and systematic conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), resulting in significant displacement of women, girls, men and children into neighbouring countries. Sudanese survivors of CRSV both within Sudan and in displaced countries face ongoing protection risks including insecurity, stigma, discrimination, retaliation, exploitation, restricted access to services, and limited opportunities to participate safely in decisions affecting their lives. The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation has been implementing the ‘Our Voice, Our Justice’ (OVOJ) project from June 2026 up to December 2028. The project is supporting Sudanese refugee CRSV survivors to organise in survivor-led networks, access protection and psychosocial support, and safely engage in advocacy for accountability and justice. The overarching goal of this project is that conflict-related sexual violence survivors from Sudan are protected and supported to safely claim their rights and advocate for justice and accountability through the strengthening of survivor networks. job.title: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala
job.location: Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa Starting Date : ASAP. COUNTRY PROFILE Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country. JOB PROFILE The Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist position is based in Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa. The position is fully dedicated to the Ethiopia mission and will report directly to the Deputy Country Representative. The postholder will lead the mission’s data team, coordinating its work across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units in close collaboration with Research Managers, the GIS Specialist and relevant HQ technical teams. The postholder will provide technical leadership and backstopping throughout the research cycle, from methodology and sampling design to data collection, cleaning, analysis, validation and dissemination. The role is responsible for coordinating data officers and interns, agreeing priorities and resource needs with Research Managers, maintaining reusable analysis systems, and ensuring compliance with IMPACT research standards and data protection requirements. The appointment level will depend on the selected candidate’s experience and technical skills, both profiles will carry responsibility for leading the data team. During the assignment, the Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist will be hosted by Acted, IMPACT's global partner, and will be under the responsibility of its delegates for all administrative, security, logistics and financial matters. The postholder will fully comply with Acted and IMPACT rules and procedures, including those relating to data protection and information security. RESPONSIBILITIES Planning and coordination: Estimate deadlines and resource requirements for each research cycle across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units. Coordinate team members’ workloads, agree data team priorities with Research Managers, and flag risks, capacity gaps and delays early, in writing, to the relevant Research Managers and direct manager. Research design: Support assessment teams in designing methodologies, sampling strategies (including sample size calculations and survey weighting), data analysis plans and data collection tools, in line with IMPACT research standards. Data collection and cleaning: Oversee the review, testing and deployment of XLSForms on IMPACT’s Kobo server, data checks during collection, and data cleaning in line with IMPACT’s Data Cleaning Minimum Standards. Where relevant, train enumerators and partner staff on data checks and cleaning. Analysis systems: Maintain and develop the mission’s R-based cleaning and analysis workflows, including IMPACT R packages, templates and Shiny applications, under version control and with up-to-date documentation so that they can be reused across research cycles. Information products: Review country-level information products and dissemination strategies to maximise the use of findings, in accordance with IMPACT research standards and in close coordination with the direct manager. Data quality: Improve data quality and monitoring at country level, including resolving discrepancies, keeping geospatial and administrative reference data up to date in coordination with GIS colleagues, and ensuring collected data is correctly georeferenced. Data protection: Ensure compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOP on personally identifiable information in all research cycles. This includes anonymisation and disclosure-risk checks before any dataset is shared, secure transfer, storage and deletion of data, and compliance with data-sharing or data processing agreements with partners. Capacity building: Lead the development and implementation of an ongoing capacity-building plan for country data officers and interns, with support from relevant technical colleagues and HQ teams. Provide training, mentoring and regular feedback on data cleaning, analysis and tools, and coordinate with Research Managers on staff development and performance. Partner engagement: At the request of the line manager, support partners on data processing, data sharing and the use of findings, and represent IMPACT on data matters in relevant coordination forums. DELIVERABLES Lead weekly data team meetings, maintain a shared task tracker with clear responsibilities and agreed timelines, and follow up on progress and outstanding actions. Provide technical guidance to data officers and interns on cleaning, analysis and troubleshooting, implement and track the capacity-building plan, and provide input to their performance appraisals in coordination with Research Managers. Regularly liaise with project focal points and Research Managers to monitor deadlines and resource needs, anticipate delays, and communicate risks and agreed corrective actions in writing. Conduct internal technical validation of all research cycles, including review of sampling, data collection tools, cleaning and analysis outputs, to ensure alignment with IMPACT/HQ guidelines before submission to HQ for validation. Ensure regular maintenance of all mission dashboards, including Power BI and Shiny, and contribute to the design and development of new dashboards when required. Keep documentation, including READMEs, SOPs and decision logs, up to date for all workflows and dashboards maintained by the data team, with code under version control and clear maintenance responsibilities. For every dataset shared outside IMPACT, document the anonymisation applied, disclosure-risk checks and transfer, in line with the relevant agreement and applicable IMPACT procedures. REQUIRED SKILLSET At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in data management and analysis, preferably in humanitarian settings. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as statistics, data science or social sciences, is preferred. Fluency in English is required. Excellent communication and data visualisation skills. Strong skills in R and in data cleaning and survey analysis workflows, familiarity with IMPACT’s R packages is an asset. Proven skills in Power BI and R Shiny. Experience with KoboToolbox or ODK and XLSForm design. Sound knowledge of sampling methods, sample size calculations and survey weighting. Experience with Git/GitHub, GIS skills in QGIS or ArcGIS are an asset. Knowledge of humanitarian data protection practice, including anonymisation of microdata and disclosure-risk assessment. Experience supervising or mentoring data staff, including remotely. Ability to manage multiple priorities across many research cycles, at times under tight deadlines. Strong ability to work independently in support of colleagues and partners. Ability to work in an intercultural environment. Previous experience in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa is highly preferred. Background Under its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation strategic priority area, CRS Uganda supports nature-based solutions, climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods. Forest Flavors (FF) is a 3-year initiative (FY26 - FY29) that applies a market systems development (MSD) and private-sector-led approach to strengthen inclusive, commercially viable and nature-positive agroforestry value chains, with an initial focus on coffee, cocoa, vanilla and spices. The project seeks to improve smallholder and dioceses market participation and returns, support enterprises to test and scale inclusive business models, and strengthen climate-resilient agroforestry landscapes. Forest Flavors will work mainly across 3 regions namely, Central region covering Luwero, Masaka and Lugazi, Western region covering Kasese and Northern region covering Gulu directly engaging with private sector actors, smallholder farmers and their organizations, service providers, financial institutions and relevant public and civil-society stakeholders to address market-system constraints and crowd in sustainable investment. Church and diocesan assets where feasible will contribute to viable business and landscape models where land tenure, governance, user rights, market demand and the business case are validated. The project will use a diagnose, prioritize, co-create, invest, learn and scale approach, with decisions guided by commercial viability, inclusion, environmental contribution and the potential for replication. Job Summary: Based in CRS Uganda’s Kampala office, the Senior Project Officer (SPO) - Private Sector Engagement and Markets will coordinate and support the implementation of Forest Flavors (FF) activities under the Church Lands and Private Sector Engagement (CL3) project. The role will focus on diocesan and private sector engagement, business development service delivery, and facilitating linkages to key market enablers, including finance, technical assistance, standards and certification bodies, and other relevant service providers. The SPO will identify and engage potential private sector actors (PSAs), in coordination with the Project Manager - CL3, and facilitate the co-creation of commercially viable, inclusive and nature-positive agroforestry business models. This will include identifying partnership opportunities to address systemic market constraints, coordinating business case development and tailored business development services, and supporting capacity strengthening in marketing, financial management and inclusive business practices. The SPO will also coordinate and follow up on activities implemented through private sector partners, verify and manage milestones, budgets and deliverables, and ensure timely activity implementation and reporting. Through effective coordination, facilitation and relationship management, the SPO will support market linkages, strengthen enterprise, diocese and smallholder participation in priority agroforestry value chains, and contribute to continuous learning and improved project results. The role will work closely with the Project Manager - CL3 and the wider FF team, as well as relevant technical, MEAL, finance and operations colleagues. This is a technical coordination role and has no direct staff supervisory responsibilities. Roles and Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning, coordination, and high-quality implementation of assigned activities in alignment with approved annual workplans, budgets, and CRS program quality standards. This includes mapping and onboarding potential Private Sector Actors (PSAs), collaborating with stakeholders to co-create commercially viable business models across priority value chains (coffee, vanilla, and spices), and maintaining rigorous activity trackers to manage deliverables, risks, and implementation milestones. Coordinate technical assistance and business development support for private sector partners / MSMEs and, dioceses based on identified needs and follow up on agreed actions to strengthen commercial performance, market access and investment readiness. Ensure, gender equality, youth inclusion and social inclusion are considered in partner diagnostics, business model design, service delivery, access to assets and finance, and tracking of economic benefits.
